title: II-A Continuity Analysis and Key Item Status Correction
use_cases: Use when identifying narrative inconsistencies in multi-episode datasets
Implement when state transitions for items must be validated against previous history
Configure when preventing incorrect item updates after a destruction event
Use when GPT-4 analysis yields contradictory state summaries for persistent objects
content: By extracting key parts of GPT-4’s analysis, we identify instances where an item reappears in later episodes after being marked as lost or destroyed, without narrative explanation. Let Si​(t)S_{i}(t) represent the state of item ii at time tt, where Si​(t)∈{active,lost,destroyed}S_{i}(t)\in\{\text{active},\text{lost},\text{destroyed}\}. If item ii reappears at time tkt_{k} with Si​(tk)=activeS_{i}(t_{k})=\text{active} after being previously marked as Si​(tk−1)∈{lost,destroyed}S_{i}(t_{k-1})\in\{\text{lost},\text{destroyed}\}, we flag this as a continuity error. To maintain consistency, the state remains Si​(tk−1)S_{i}(t_{k-1}), avoiding an incorrect update. This approach systematically corrects discrepancies in item states, ensuring that narrative continuity is preserved by preventing erroneous state transitions.
